candidates.name: Developing estates: plan requirements and surveying specification (Practice Guide 41, supplement 5)
verified_facts: Estate plans must be based on an accurate survey plotted to the stated scale.
HMLR specifies plottable accuracy of 0.3 mm at map scale plus one part in one thousand of measured distance.
The preferred estate-plan scale is 1:500, with 1:1250 acceptable where detail remains clear.
Survey control stations should preserve the datum used for the original survey and final as-built work.
semantic_limits: These estate-plan tolerances are plan/survey acceptance criteria and are not a substitute for parcel LiDAR elevation uncertainty or exact legal-boundary proof.

candidates.name: Developing estates: estate boundary approval (Practice Guide 41, supplement 1)
verified_facts: Boundary approval requires a site survey plan prepared by a land surveyor.
HMLR compares the external boundaries on the site survey plan with the registered title and the latest Ordnance Survey map.
Survey notes describing physical external boundaries help reconcile survey detail with Ordnance Survey mapping.
semantic_limits: Reconciliation to the latest OS map improves plan consistency but does not turn mapped physical detail into exact legal-boundary coordinates or elevation samples.
